agent_note: HIGH CONFIDENCE PAST. 21 event quotes, 20 past / 1 present (95.2% past). 27 gnomic, 7 dialogue, 3 unclear. NO SINGLE QUOTE FLIPS THE LABEL: q05512 is the lone present quote, and reclassifying it as gnomic or dialogue would make the book 20 of 20 past - still HIGH CONFIDENCE PAST. Nothing else moves it either. NOT in the 70-85% present band. Multiple narrators (third-person past around Emmett and Woolly, first-person past for Duchess and Sally); the unifying evidence is unfakeable specific-scene past narration - 'he looked at me and waited', 'Mr. Kehlenbeck had gone to the chalkboard, scratched out a formula'. THE MAIN BUCKETING WORK HERE was resisting the gnomic over-application METHODOLOGY warns about, and this book is dense with the trap: q05483 ('being grateful was one thing, and being beholden, that was another'), q05486 ('a farmer with a mortgage was like a man walking on the railing of a bridge'), q05495 ('the whiskey bottle was sort of like a pencil with eraser') and q05509's has-been passage all READ as aphorism but are PAST-tense, so they are event-narration, not gnomic. Filing those four as gnomic would have cut the event count from 21 to 17 and is exactly the 54%-precision error mode described in METHODOLOGY. Separately, reported THOUGHT with a past tag ('thought Woolly', 'I thought to myself' - q05463, q05466, q05471) I treated as event/past rather than dialogue, since the dialogue bucket is defined as character SPEECH; long tagged speech (q05476, q05484) went to dialogue on the speech-majority precedence rule. THREE FLAGGED CASES for the methodology, not just this book: (1) q05507 is METHODOLOGY's own documented contested exception - past-tense REAL-world historical exposition used as argument by analogy with no story character - flagged rather than decided silently. (2) q05519 is a 450-word essayistic passage carrying one interpolated past narration clause; I called it gnomic, but as event/past the book would be 21 of 22. (3) q05512 exposes a genuine gap: PRESENT-tense habitual exposition about a specific story-world character, with no specific story-moment. METHODOLOGY rules on the past-tense version of this (Molenbeek, 'Such was life in the caliphate' - both event) but says nothing about the present-tense mirror, which falls between the gnomic definition (requires generalizing BEYOND the story world - this does not) and the event definition (requires a specific story-MOMENT - this has none). I hit the same undocumented category twice more in Picoult (q05969, q05989). It needs a ruling. Dedup misses: q05517 is the severed tail of q05518 (a scraping artifact, should be merged), and q05513 partially echoes q05477.
